summary.title: Software Engineering at Google
summary.one_liner: Learn how Google structures its software engineering practices, covering its unified source repository, the Blaze build system, code review, testing, bug tracking, and language policies.
takeaways: Google keeps most code in one unified repository, where engineers can read and build almost any code, with owners approving changes to their subtrees.
The Blaze build system uses hermetic, deterministic build steps and distributed, cached builds so that builds and tests are fast and reliable.
Code review is mandatory: every change needs at least one other reviewer, and owners must approve changes to their code, with automated presubmit tests.
Development happens at the head of the repository rather than on branches, with a build cop and a green-build focus to keep integration problems small.
Google restricts official languages to C++, Java, Python, Go and JavaScript, and uses style guides and readability training to keep code consistent.
summary.summary: This paper by Fergus Henderson, a Google software engineer, catalogs the key software engineering practices used at Google. It is organized by topic, starting with software development (source repository, build system, code review, testing, bug tracking, languages, debugging, release engineering, launch approval, post-mortems, and rewrites), then covers project management (20% time, OKRs, project approval, reorganizations, hack weeks) and people management (roles, facilities, training, transfers, performance appraisal). The approach is descriptive: it explains each practice briefly and includes concrete figures, such as repository size and commit rates, and notes where practices have since changed.
